key_insight: The paper reframes pressure as a geometric potential that curves an effective space, unifying pressure-driven motion and vortex identification through curvature-based invariants.
engineering_relevance: This gives fluid engineers a new physics-based lens for interpreting vortices, pressure fields, and 2D turbulence cascades in CFD and flow diagnostics.
method: Build a Newton-Cartan geometric framework for pressure.
Apply a conformal transformation to define an effective curved spatial metric.
Relate vortex criteria to Ricci/Einstein-like curvature invariants and geodesic motion.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical derivation rather than a data-driven benchmark, showing consistency with the Euler equation, the pressure Poisson equation, and 2D topological constraints.
watch_item: The framework is largely conceptual and geometric, so practical use will depend on how robustly the curvature quantities can be computed from noisy experimental or simulation data.
paper_title: On the relationships between pressure geometrization and vortex identification
